Three athletes from [[India]] qualified for the [[2014 Winter Olympics]] in [[Sochi]], Russia, held between 7 and 23 February 2014. The country's participation in Sochi marked its ninth appearance at the Winter Olympics since its debut in [[India at the 1964 Winter Olympics|1964]].{{efn|name= Chamonix|The first medals for [[Alpinism at the Olympic Games|alpinism]] were awarded at closing ceremony of the [[1924 Winter Olympics]] in [[Chamonix]], to the members of the unsuccessful [[1922 British Mount Everest expedition]] led by [[Charles Granville Bruce]].<ref>{{cite web|first1=Volker|last1=Kluge|first2=Thomas|last2=Lippert|title=The Olympic Alpinism Prize and a promise redeemed|work=International Society of Olympic Historians|date=2013|url=https://isoh.org/wp-content/uploads/JOH-Archives/JOHv21n3n.pdf|access-date=27 January 2024|archive-date=27 January 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240127200156/https://isoh.org/wp-content/uploads/JOH-Archives/JOHv21n3n.pdf|url-status=bot: unknown}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Charles Granville Bruce | work=[[British Olympic Association]]|url=https://www.teamgb.com/athlete/charles-granville-bruce/4y9AOl4OjHnTXniIPKVh4T|access-date=1 January 2024}}</ref> The medals were awarded to 21 people: the [[1922 British Mount Everest expedition#Expedition participants|thirteen British expedition members]], seven Indian [[Sherpas]] who died during the ascent and one Nepalese soldier.<ref name="IW"/><ref>{{cite web|last=Douglas |first=Ed|title='My modest father never mentioned his Everest expedition Olympic gold'|work=[[The Guardian]]|date=19 May 2012|url=https://www.theguardian.com/world/2012/may/19/olympic-secret-everest-forgotten-hero|access-date=28 January 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Olympic Prize Alpinism|work=The Gurkha Museum, Winchester|date=12 January 2021|url=https://thegurkhamuseum.co.uk/blog/olympic-prize-alpinism/|access-date=28 January 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Olympedia – Alpinism| work=[[Olympedia]]|url=https://www.olympedia.org/sports/APN|access-date=28 January 2024}}</ref> As the medal was awarded to a team of players of various nationalities, the [[International Olympic Committee]] recognizes it as a medal awarded to the [[Mixed teams at the Olympics|mixed team]] rather than any individual nation.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://olympics.com/en/olympic-games/chamonix-1924/medals|title=Chamonix 1924 Olympic Medal Table|work=[[International Olympic Committee]]|access-date=15 August 2024}}</ref>}}

While three Indians qualified for the games, they entered the competition as [[Independent Olympic Participants at the 2014 Winter Olympics|Independent Olympic Participants]] due to the suspension of the [[Indian Olympic Association]] since 2012. After [[Shiva Keshavan]] had participated in the [[Luge at the 2014 Winter Olympics|luge]] event on 11 February 2014, the [[International Olympic Committee]] reinstated India's [[National Olympic Committee]] (NOC). This allowed the other two athletes, [[Himanshu Thakur]] and [[Nadeem Iqbal]], who still had their respective events to compete under the Indian flag.

As participation under the Indian flag was not approved initially, there was no official flag-bearer during the [[2014 Winter Olympics opening ceremony|opening ceremony]]. Thakur served as the flag-bearer during the [[2014 Winter Olympics closing ceremony|closing ceremony]]. India did not win a medal, and as of these Games, India had not earned a Winter Olympic medal.

== Background ==
The [[Indian Olympic Association]] was recognized by the [[International Olympic Committee]] in 1927.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.olympic.org/india|title=India – National Olympic Committee (NOC)|work=[[International Olympic Committee]]|access-date=1 July 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180326005433/https://www.olympic.org/india/|archive-date=26 March 2018|url-status=live|df=dmy-all}}</ref> However, by this time, they had already competed in three [[Summer Olympic Games]], in [[1900 Summer Olympics|1900]], [[1920 Summer Olympics|1920]], and [[1924 Summer Olympics|1924]]. The nation made its first Winter Olympics appearance until the [[1964 Winter Olympics]] held in [[Innsbruck]], Austria.{{efn|name= Chamonix}}<ref name="IW">{{cite web|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/countries/IND/|title=India at the Olympics|work=Sports Reference|access-date=30 July 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180108233500/https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/countries/IND/|archive-date=8 January 2018|url-status=dead|df=dmy-all}}</ref> This edition of the Games marked the nation's ninth appearance at the [[Winter Olympics]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://olympics.com/en/news/india-winter-olympics-history-athletes-list-qualify|title=India at Winter Olympics - Jeremy Bujakowski to Arif Khan|work=[[Olympics.com]]|access-date=1 June 2024|archive-date=21 July 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240721162720/https://olympics.com/en/news/india-winter-olympics-history-athletes-list-qualify|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.olympedia.org/countries/IND|title=India at the Olympics|work=[[Olympedia]]|access-date=1 June 2024|archive-date=10 October 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231010142456/http://www.olympedia.org/countries/IND|url-status=live}}</ref>

The [[Indian Olympic Association]] (IOA) was suspended by the [[International Olympic Committee]] (IOC) due to government interference in the autonomy of the country's [[National Olympic Committee]] (NOC) in December 2012.<ref>{{cite news |date=4 December 2012 |title=IOC bans India from Olympics |url=http://www.cbc.ca/sports/ioc-bans-india-from-olympics-1.1272480 |work=[[CBC Sports]] |access-date=31 December 2013 |archive-date=1 January 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140101104608/http://www.cbc.ca/sports/ioc-bans-india-from-olympics-1.1272480 |url-status=live }}</ref> It was announced on 31 December 2013 that India would be competing under the [[Olympic flag]] in Sochi.<ref>{{cite news |date=10 January 2014 |title=Three Indians to take part in Sochi Winter Games |url=http://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/sports/tournaments/2014-sochi-winter-olympics/Three-Indians-to-take-part-in-Sochi-Winter-Games/articleshow/28596848.cms |newspaper=[[The Times of India]] |access-date=10 January 2014 |archive-date=29 November 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151129170218/http://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/sports/tournaments/2014-sochi-winter-olympics/Three-Indians-to-take-part-in-Sochi-Winter-Games/articleshow/28596848.cms |url-status=live }}</ref> [[Shiva Keshavan]] had traveled to [[Sochi]] independently and the skiing team consisting of athletes [[Himanshu Thakur]], and [[Nadeem Iqbal]] and three coaches traveled from [[Delhi]] to Sochi on 5 February 2014.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/india/Indian-skiers-off-to-Russia-to-take-part-in-Olympics-without-national-flag/articleshow/29833899.cms|title=Indian skiers off o Russia to take part in Olympics|date=4 February 2014|access-date=1 June 2024|newspaper=[[The Times of India]]|archive-date=21 July 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240721162731/https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/india/Indian-skiers-off-to-Russia-to-take-part-in-Olympics-without-national-flag/articleshow/29833899.cms|url-status=live}}</ref> As participation under the Indian flag was not approved, there was no official flag-bearer during the [[2014 Winter Olympics opening ceremony|opening ceremony]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.olympic.org/Documents/Games_Sochi_2014/Flagbearers_Sochi_2014_Opening_Ceremony.pdf|title=Sochi 2014 Opening Ceremony|date=7 February 2014|work=[[International Olympic Committee]]|access-date=7 February 2014|archive-date=26 March 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140326222842/http://www.olympic.org/Documents/Games_Sochi_2014/Flagbearers_Sochi_2014_Opening_Ceremony.pdf|url-status=live}}</ref>

Elections for the Indian Olympic Association were scheduled two days after the [[2014 Winter Olympics opening ceremony|opening ceremony]], which was the major condition for the suspension to be lifted.<ref>{{cite news |date=31 December 2013 |title=Sochi Games: Four Indian skiers to go as independent athletes |url=http://zeenews.india.com/sports/others/sochi-games-four-indian-skiers-to-go-as-independent-athletes_777046.html |work=[[Zee news]] |access-date=31 December 2013 |archive-date=2 January 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140102160545/http://zeenews.india.com/sports/others/sochi-games-four-indian-skiers-to-go-as-independent-athletes_777046.html |url-status=live }}</ref> The [[International Olympic Committee]] eventually reinstated the Indian Olympic Association on 11 February after the election of a new board headed by [[Narayana Ramachandran]], the president of the [[World Squash Federation]], who was voted in as its new president.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://edition.cnn.com/2014/02/11/world/asia/sochi-olympics-india-reinstated/index.html?hpt=hp_t2 |title=International Olympic Committee reinstates India at Sochi after ban |work=[[CNN]] |date=11 February 2014 |access-date=11 February 2014 |archive-date=22 February 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140222091016/http://edition.cnn.com/2014/02/11/world/asia/sochi-olympics-india-reinstated/index.html?hpt=hp_t2 |url-status=live }}</ref> By then, Keshavan had already participated in the [[Luge at the 2014 Winter Olympics|luge]] event on 11 February 2014 as an [[Independent Olympic Participants at the 2014 Winter Olympics|Independent Olympic Participant]].<ref name="NDTV">{{cite news |title=Sochi 2014: India's Shiva Keshavan registers worst Winter Olympics performance, finishes 37th |url=https://sports.ndtv.com/othersports/sochi-2014-indias-shiva-keshavan-registers-worst-winter-olympics-performance-finishes-37th-1523581?|agency=[[Press Trust of India]] |work=[[NDTV]] |date=10 February 2014 |access-date=21 February 2014 |archive-date=2 March 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140302090246/http://sports.ndtv.com/othersports/othersports/220693-sochi-2014-indias-shiva-keshavan-registers-worst-winter-olympics-performance-finishes-37th |url-status=live }}</ref>

The other two athletes [[Himanshu Thakur]] and [[Nadeem Iqbal]], who still had pending events were able to compete under the Indian flag.<ref name="IT">{{cite news|url=https://www.indiatoday.in/sports/other-sports/story/sochi-games-indian-tricolour-unfurled-181309-2014-02-16|title=Sochi Games: Tricolour unfurled, Indian teams can now proudly fly national flag and wear dresses with India written on them|date=16 February 2014|access-date=1 June 2024|work=[[India Today]]|archive-date=21 July 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240721162728/https://www.indiatoday.in/sports/other-sports/story/sochi-games-indian-tricolour-unfurled-181309-2014-02-16|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="Result">{{cite web|url=https://www.olympedia.org/countries/IND/editions/58|title=India at the 2014 Winter Olympics|work=[[Olympedia]]|access-date=1 June 2024|archive-date=2 May 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240502061832/http://www.olympedia.org/countries/IND/editions/58|url-status=live}}</ref> On 16 February 2014, the [[Indian flag]] was hoisted in the Games village by the newly IOA president in the presence of IOC officials and the Indian delegation.<ref name="IT"/> Thakur served as the flag-bearer during the [[2014 Winter Olympics closing ceremony|closing ceremony]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Sochi 2014 Closing Ceremony - Flagbearers |url=http://www.olympic.org/Documents/Games_Sochi_2014/Flagbearers_Sochi_2014_Closing_Ceremony.pdf |work=[[International Olympic Committee]] |date=23 February 2014 |access-date=23 February 2014 |archive-date=27 March 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140327092930/http://www.olympic.org/Documents/Games_Sochi_2014/Flagbearers_Sochi_2014_Closing_Ceremony.pdf |url-status=live }}</ref>

== Alpine skiing ==
=== Qualification ===
{{main article|Alpine skiing at the 2014 Winter Olympics – Qualification}}

The basic qualification mark for [[Alpine skiing at the 2014 Winter Olympics – Men's slalom|slalom]] and [[Alpine skiing at the 2014 Winter Olympics – Men's giant slalom|giant slalom]] events stipulated an average of less than 140 points in the list published by the [[International Ski Federation]] (FIS) as of 19 January 2014 for competitors ranked outside the top 100. The quotas were allocated further based on athletes satisfying other criteria, with a maximum of 22 athletes (maximum of 14 male or 14 female athletes) from a single participating NOC with not more than four participants in a single event.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fis-ski.com/DB/media/olympic-games/sochi2014-18-09-2012-qualification-system-fis-english.pdf|title=2014 Winter Olympics Alpine Skiing Selection Procedure|work=[[International Ski Federation]]|access-date=1 June 2024|archive-date=10 February 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220210091417/https://www.fis-ski.com/DB/media/olympic-games/sochi2014-18-09-2012-qualification-system-fis-english.pdf|url-status=live}}</ref> As per the final quota allocation released on 20 January 2014,<ref name="Quota">{{cite web |url=http://data.fis-ski.com/media/olympic-games/quota-20-01-2014-6.pdf |title=Summary of Quota allocation as per 20.01.2014 |date=20 January 2014 |publisher=[[International Ski Federation]] |access-date=31 January 2014 |archive-date=29 January 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140129014759/http://data.fis-ski.com/media/olympic-games/quota-20-01-2014-6.pdf |url-status=live }}</ref> In December 2013, Indian [[alpine skiing|alpine skiers]] Himanshu Thakur and [[Hira Lal (skier)|Hira Lal]] achieved the basic qualification mark for the giant slalom event.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.indiatoday.in/sports/story/indian-athletes-sochi-winter-olympics-ioa-ioc-175804-2014-01-06|title=No Indian flag at Winter Olympics, country's athletes to compete as independent sportspersons|date=7 January 2014|access-date=1 June 2024|work=[[India Today]]|archive-date=21 July 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240721162619/https://www.indiatoday.in/sports/story/indian-athletes-sochi-winter-olympics-ioa-ioc-175804-2014-01-06|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/punjab/3-manali-skiers-qualify-for-winter-olympics/story-iQrlyjfmG0gEjetSlhGhFJ.html|title=3 Manali skiers qualify for Winter Olympics|date=21 December 2013|access-date=1 June 2024|newspaper=[[The Hindustan Times]]}}</ref>

Despite two athletes achieving the qualification standard, India was allocated only one quota place based on the allocation criteria.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://data.fis-ski.com/dynamic/assigned-quota-for-olympic-games-2014-sochi.html?sectorcode=al |title=Alpine skiing quotas list for Olympic Winter Games 2022 |date=20 January 2014|work=[[International Ski Federation]] |access-date=20 November 2014 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140202171422/http://data.fis-ski.com/dynamic/assigned-quota-for-olympic-games-2014-sochi.html?sectorcode=al|archive-date=2 February 2014}}</ref> Though Lal had prior experience having participated in the [[2006 Turin Olympics]], Thakur was selected for the event on account of his better performances in the recent events.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/2014-sochi-winter-olympics/three-indians-to-take-part-in-sochi-winter-games/articleshow/28596848.cms|title=Three Indians to take part in Sochi Winter Games|date=9 January 2014|access-date=1 June 2024|newspaper=[[The Times of India]]|archive-date=21 July 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240721162622/https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/2014-sochi-winter-olympics/three-indians-to-take-part-in-sochi-winter-games/articleshow/28596848.cms|url-status=live}}</ref> The 20-year old Thakur hailed from [[Manali, Himachal Pradesh|Manali]] in the [[States and union territories of India|Indian state]] [[Himachal Pradesh]] and is a younger cousin of Lal.<ref name="Independent">{{cite news|url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/olympics/news/in-from-the-cold-india-has-been-officially-excluded-from-the-sochi-winter-olympic-games-but-four-of-its-athletes-will-still-compete-9081510.html|title=In from the cold: India has been officially excluded from the Sochi Winter Olympic Games but four of its athletes will still compete|date=23 January 2014|access-date=1 June 2024|newspaper=[[The Independent]]}}</ref>

=== Main event ===
{{main article|Alpine skiing at the 2014 Winter Olympics}}

Thakur was initially slated to compete as an Independent athlete at the games.<ref name="DNA">{{cite news|url=https://www.dnaindia.com/sports/report-two-alpine-skiers-and-a-luger-qualify-for-sochi-winter-olympics-won-t-be-able-to-carry-indian-flag-though-1951782|title=Two Alpine skiers and a luger qualify for Sochi Winter Olympics; won't be able to carry Indian flag though|date=29 September 2017|access-date=1 June 2024|newspaper=[[Daily News and Analysis]]|archive-date=21 July 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240721163221/https://www.dnaindia.com/sports/report-two-alpine-skiers-and-a-luger-qualify-for-sochi-winter-olympics-won-t-be-able-to-carry-indian-flag-though-1951782|url-status=live}}</ref> But after the reinstatement of the Indian Olympic Committee on 11 February 2014, he received the necessary funding and equipment from the [[Government of India]] two days later, less than a week before the main event.<ref>{{cite news|date=13 February 2014|title=Sochi Olympics: Indian Himanshu Thakur gets skiing gear just in time|url=https://www.firstpost.com/sports/sochi-olympics-indian-himanshu-thakur-gets-skiing-gear-just-in-time-1389059.html|access-date=2 January 2022|newspaper=[[Firstpost]]|archive-date=21 February 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220221212521/https://www.firstpost.com/sports/sochi-olympics-indian-himanshu-thakur-gets-skiing-gear-just-in-time-1389059.html|url-status=live}}</ref> The giant slalom event was held on 19 February 2014 at the [[Rosa Khutor Alpine Resort]] and marked Thakur's first and only appearance at the Winter Olympic Games.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://olympics.com/en/athletes/himanshu-thakur|title=Himanshu Thakur|work=[[Olympics.com]]|access-date=1 June 2024|archive-date=21 July 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240721163204/https://olympics.com/en/athletes/himanshu-thakur|url-status=live}}</ref> Thakur completed his first run in 1:47.86 to rank 71st. He took slightly longer to complete the course in the second run at 1:49.69 to be ranked 72nd among the competition.<ref name="AS">{{cite report|url=https://medias4.fis-ski.com/pdf/2014/AL/0342/2014AL0342RLR2.pdf|title=Results of Alpine skiing at the 2014 Winter Olympics – Men's giant slalom|work=[[International Ski Federation]]|date=13 February 2022|access-date=1 June 2024|archive-date=3 July 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240703034504/http://medias4.fis-ski.com/pdf/2014/AL/0342/2014AL0342RLR2.pdf|url-status=live}}</ref> With a combined time of 3:37.55, he finished 72nd and last amongst the classified finishers in the overall classification.<ref name="AS"/><ref>{{cite news |title=India end 2014 Winter Olympics campaign as skier Himanshu Thakur finishes last |url=http://sports.ndtv.com/othersports/othersports/221120-india-end-2014-winter-olympics-campaign-as-skier-himanshu-thakur-finishes-last |agency=[[Reuters]] |work=[[NDTV]] |date=20 February 2014 |access-date=21 February 2014 |archive-date=11 March 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140311141535/http://sports.ndtv.com/othersports/othersports/221120-india-end-2014-winter-olympics-campaign-as-skier-himanshu-thakur-finishes-last |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.olympedia.org/results/350002|title=Giant Slalom, Men|work=[[Olympedia]]|access-date=1 June 2024|archive-date=19 August 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230819111816/https://www.olympedia.org/results/350002|url-status=live}}</ref>

== Cross-country skiing ==
=== Qualification ===
{{main article|Cross-country skiing at the 2014 Winter Olympics – Qualification}}

As per the "A" standard, athletes with a maximum of 100 distance points were allowed to compete in both the sprint and distance events. Athletes with a maximum of 120 sprint points were allowed to compete in the sprint event. They were also allowed to compete in the distance event provided that their distance points did not exceed 300. NOCs which did not have any athlete meeting the "A" standard were allowed to enter one competitor of each sex (known as the basic quota) in the sprint event or the distance event provided that they satisfied the "B" standard of having a maximum of 300 distance points at the end of qualifying on 20 January 2014. A maximum of 20 athletes (maximum of 12 male or 12 female athletes) from a single participating NOC were allowed to compete and the remaining quotas were allocated further to athletes satisfying the "B" standard criteria from other NOCs.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fis-ski.com/data/document/fis-sochi2014-180912.pdf |title=Qualification Systems for XXII Olympic Winter Games, Sochi 2014 |work=[[International Ski Federation]] |access-date=10 November 2012 |archive-url=https://www.webcitation.org/6Dj2DaqNh?url=http://www.fis-ski.com/data/document/fis-sochi2014-180912.pdf |archive-date=16 January 2013 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

Indian skier Nadeem Iqbal achieved the basic qualification mark to participate in the [[Cross-country skiing at the 2014 Winter Olympics&nbsp;– Men's 15 kilometre classical|Men's 15 km classical]] distance event at the Nordic qualifying ski event held at France and Italy in November–December.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://indianexpress.com/article/news-archive/web/on-the-slopes-of-kashmir-a-soldier-trains-for-olympic-medal-in-sochi/|title=On the slopes of Kashmir, a soldier trains for Olympic medal in Sochi|date=5 January 2014|access-date=1 June 2024|newspaper=[[The Indian Express]]|archive-date=21 July 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240721163123/https://indianexpress.com/article/news-archive/web/on-the-slopes-of-kashmir-a-soldier-trains-for-olympic-medal-in-sochi/|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.business-standard.com/article/pti-stories/four-indians-qualify-for-sochi-winter-games-113121800614_1.html|title=Four Indians qualify for Sochi Winter Games|date=8 December 2013|access-date=1 June 2024|newspaper=[[Business Standard]]|archive-date=21 July 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240721163125/https://www.business-standard.com/article/pti-stories/four-indians-qualify-for-sochi-winter-games-113121800614_1.html|url-status=live}}</ref> As per the final quota allocation released on 20 January 2014, India was allocated one place for the distance event under the basic quota.<ref name="Quota"/><ref>{{cite web |url=http://data.fis-ski.com/dynamic/assigned-quota-for-olympic-games-2014-sochi.html?sectorcode=cc |title=Alpine skiing quotas list for Olympic Winter Games 2022 |date=20 January 2014|publisher=[[International Ski Federation]] |access-date=20 November 2014 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140410013053/http://data.fis-ski.com/dynamic/assigned-quota-for-olympic-games-2014-sochi.html?sectorcode=cc|archive-date=10 April 2014}}</ref> Iqbal hailed from [[Gulmarg]] in the Indian state of [[Jammu and Kashmir (state)|Jammu and Kashmir]].<ref name="Independent"/> He is the first athlete representing the [[Indian Army]] from the state to qualify for the Winter Olympic Games.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://sports.ndtv.com/othersports/sochi-2014-nadeem-iqbal-becomes-first-soldier-from-jk-to-qualify-for-winter-olympics-1523419?|title=Sochi 2014: Nadeem Iqbal becomes first soldier from J&K to qualify for Winter Olympics|date=13 February 2014|access-date=1 June 2014|work=[[NDTV]]|archive-date=21 July 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240721163157/https://sports.ndtv.com/othersports/sochi-2014-nadeem-iqbal-becomes-first-soldier-from-jk-to-qualify-for-winter-olympics-1523419?|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |date=13 February 2014 |title=Nadeem first soldier from J&K to qualify for Winter Olympics |url=http://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/sports/tournaments/2014-sochi-winter-olympics/Nadeem-first-soldier-from-JK-to-qualify-for-Winter-Olympics/articleshow/30352825.cms |newspaper=[[Times of India]] |access-date=13 February 2014 |archive-date=18 February 2022 === Main event ===
[[File:Надеем_Икбал.JPG|thumb|[[Nadeem Iqbal]] during the [[Cross-country skiing at the 2014 Winter Olympics – Men's 15 kilometre classical|cross-country event]]]]
{{further|Cross-country skiing at the 2014 Winter Olympics}}

Iqbal was initially slated to compete as an Independent athlete at the games.<ref name="DNA"/> But after the reinstatement of the Indian Olympic Committee on 11 February 2014, he received clearance to compete under the Indian flag the day before the main event.<ref name="IT"/> The main event was held on 14 February 2014 at the [[Laura Biathlon & Ski Complex]] and marked Iqbal's first and only participation in the Winter Olympic Games.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://olympics.com/en/athletes/nadeem-iqbal|title=Nadeem Iqbal|work=[[Olympics.com]]|access-date=1 June 2024|archive-date=21 July 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240721163157/https://olympics.com/en/athletes/nadeem-iqbal|url-status=live}}</ref> Iqbal completed the {{cvt|15|km}} course in 55:12.5.<ref name="CC">{{cite web|url=http://data.fis-ski.com/pdf/2014/CC/3060/2014CC3060RL.pdf |title=Final Results - Men's 15km classical|access-date=15 February 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140220020311/http://data.fis-ski.com/pdf/2014/CC/3060/2014CC3060RL.pdf |work=[[International Ski Federation]]|archive-date=20 February 2014|url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.olympedia.org/results/350006|title=Cross-country 15km classical, Men|work=[[Olympedia]]|access-date=1 June 2024|archive-date=9 July 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240709155227/https://www.olympedia.org/results/350006|url-status=live}}</ref> He finished the race in 85th position (out of 87 competitors who completed the race), nearly 17 minutes behind the winner [[Dario Cologna]] of [[Switzerland at the 2014 Winter Olympics|Switzerland]].<ref name="IT"/><ref name="CC"/><ref>{{cite news |title=Sochi 2014: Cross-country skier Nadeem Iqbal finishes 85th in men's 15km classic run event at Winter Olympics |url=http://sports.ndtv.com/othersports/othersports/220893-sochi-2014-cross-country-skier-nadeem-iqbal-finishes-85th-in-mens-15km-classic-run-event-at-winter-olympics |agency=[[Press Trust of India]] |work=[[NDTV]] |date=14 February 2014 |access-date=14 February 2014 |archive-date=4 March 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140304213055/http://sports.ndtv.com/othersports/othersports/220893-sochi-2014-cross-country-skier-nadeem-iqbal-finishes-85th-in-mens-15km-classic-run-event-at-winter-olympics |url-status=live }}</ref>

== Luge ==
[[File:2017-12-01 Shiva Keshavan by Sandro Halank–02.jpg|thumb|upright=0.75|[[Shiva Keshavan]] qualified for the [[Luge at the 2014 Winter Olympics|luge]] event, but competed as an [[Independent Olympic Participant|independent participant]] due to the suspension of the [[Indian Olympic Committee|Indian NOC]].]]

=== Qualification ===
{{main article|Luge at the 2014 Winter Olympics – Qualification}}

As per the qualification criteria, a maximum of 38 men were eligible for qualification. The qualification was based on the cumulative world ranking points from 1 November to 31 December 2013. The top ranked 30 athletes qualified directly and eight athletes were later added with first preference given to qualified relay teams who did not qualify individuals in all three disciplines followed by athletes from NOCs that met the minimum standards and who had not already qualified any athlete.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fil-luge.org/fileadmin/user_upload/Documents/Reglement/Sochi_2014_Qualification_System.pdf |title=Qualification Systems for Luge, Sochi 2014 |work=[[International Luge Federation]] |date=15 March 2012 |access-date=10 November 2012 |archive-date=19 February 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140219001237/http://www.fil-luge.org/fileadmin/user_upload/Documents/Reglement/Sochi_2014_Qualification_System.pdf |url-status=live }}</ref> India got one of the additional quota spots, as no nations were able to use them to complete a relay.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fil-luge.org/index.php?id=439&cup_id_fk=81&L= |title=Men's Cup Results |work=[[International Luge Federation]] |access-date=10 November 2012 |archive-date=24 September 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150924051114/http://www.fil-luge.org/index.php?id=439&cup_id_fk=81&L= |url-status=live }}</ref> Shiva Keshavan was the only Indian to qualify for the event.<ref name="SK">{{cite news |title=Shiva Kesavan hopes India's suspension lifted before Sochi Olympics |url=http://olympics.cbc.ca/news/article/shiva-kesavan-hopes-india-suspension-lifted-before-sochi-olympics-30984.html |work=[[Canadian Broadcasting Corporation]] |agency=Associated Press |date=18 December 2013 |access-date=31 January 2014 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140129111156/http://olympics.cbc.ca/news/article/shiva-kesavan-hopes-india-suspension-lifted-before-sochi-olympics-30984.html |archive-date=29 January 2014 |df=dmy-all}}</ref> Keshavan had represented India since 1997 and was the youngest ever men's luge competitor at the [[1998 Nagano Olympics]], where he finished 28th. He was also the sole Indian athlete to compete at the [[2002 Winter Olympics]] and further represented India in the [[2006 Winter Olympics|2006]] and [[2010 Winter Olympics|2010]] Games.<ref name="Independent"/>

=== Main event ===
{{Main|Luge at the 2014 Winter Olympics}}
In the main event, Keshavan competed as an [[Independent Olympic Participants at the 2014 Winter Olympics|Independent Olympic Participant]] due to the suspension of the Indian NOC.<ref name="SK" /> This was Kesavan's fifth consecutive appearance at the Winter Olympic Games since he made his debut at the 1998 Nagano Olympics.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://olympics.com/en/athletes/shiva-keshavan|title=Shiva Keshavan, profile|work=[[Olympics.com]]|access-date=1 June 2024|archive-date=21 July 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240721163226/https://olympics.com/en/athletes/shiva-keshavan|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="NDTV"/>

The event was held on 11 February 2014 at the [[Sliding Center Sanki]].<ref name="Luge">{{cite report|url=https://www.fil-luge.org/filext/results/2013-2014/2013LGM_SOCOG.pdf|title=Luge at the 2014 Winter Olympics - Men's Singles|work=[[International Olympic Committee]]|access-date=1 June 2024|date=11 February 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140227025854/https://www.fil-luge.org/filext/results/2013-2014/2013LGM_SOCOG.pdf|archive-date=27 February 2014}}</ref>
In his first run, Keshavan clocked a time of 53.905, finishing 1.735 behind the leader [[Albert Demchenko]]. In the second run, he clocked 55.203 to be ranked next to last amongst the 39 participants. In the penultimate run, he completed the circuit with a slightly better time of 54.706 to be ranked 37th. He had his best run in the final attempt, finishing 34th with a time of 53.335.<ref name="Luge"/> Keshavan clocked a total time of 3:37.149 and was classified in the 37th position out of the 39 athletes, marking his worst ever performance at the Winter Olympic Games.<ref name="NDTV"/><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.olympedia.org/results/350405|title=Luge Singles, Men|work=[[Olympedia]]|access-date=1 June 2024|archive-date=2 May 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240502102153/http://www.olympedia.org/results/350405|url-status=live}}</ref>
